text: Earth to Mars orbit change is about 78 million km (Mars mean distance about 227.9 million km minus Earth about 149.6 million km)
as_written: about seventy eight million kilometres farther from the Sun
source: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center Planetary Fact Sheets (Earth and Mars)

text: Raising Earth to Mars's orbit requires about a month of the Sun's total luminosity in energy, from the difference in orbital energy using the Sun's GM, Earth's mass and a luminosity of 3.83e26 W (about 9e32 J)
as_written: roughly a month of everything the Sun radiates
source: Derived from IAU 2015 Resolution B3 nominal solar luminosity and GM_sun, with Earth's mass from the NASA Earth Fact Sheet

text: Earth's mean distance from the Sun is about 150 million km
as_written: about one hundred and fifty million kilometres from the Sun
source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, Earth

text: Mars's mean distance from the Sun is about 228 million km
as_written: about two hundred and twenty eight million
source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, Mars

text: Mars's orbital distance is about 1.52 times Earth's
as_written: one and a half times as far
source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, Mars

text: Earth's mean orbital speed is about 29.8 km/s
source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, Earth

text: Mars's mean orbital speed is about 24.1 km/s, which approximates a circular orbit speed at that distance
source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, Mars

text: Earth keeping its present speed at Mars's distance would be on an ellipse with aphelion near 5 AU, close to Jupiter's distance of about 5.2 AU
source: Derived from the vis-viva equation with NASA Planetary Fact Sheet values

text: The Moon's mean distance from Earth is about 384,400 km
as_written: about three hundred and eighty four thousand kilometres away
source: NASA Moon Fact Sheet

text: Earth's Hill sphere radius is about 1.5 million km
as_written: about one and a half million kilometres
source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet and standard Hill sphere calculation

text: Hill radius scales linearly with orbital distance, so it grows by about half at 1.52 AU
source: Hill sphere formula, derived from Kepler orbital scaling

text: Total solar irradiance at Earth is about 1361 W per square metre
as_written: one thousand three hundred and sixty one watts
source: NASA SORCE/TIM and TSIS-1 measurements; Kopp and Lean 2011

text: Irradiance at Mars's mean distance is about 590 W per square metre
source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, Mars (about 586 W/m2)

text: Irradiance at Mars distance is about 43 percent of Earth's, by inverse square law
source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet; inverse square law

text: The Sun's apparent diameter falls to about two thirds at 1.52 AU
as_written: about two thirds of its old width
source: Geometry; Sun's angular size from NASA Sun Fact Sheet

text: Sunlight takes just over 8 minutes to reach Earth
source: NASA Solar System Exploration

text: Sunlight takes nearly 13 minutes to reach Mars's distance (about 12.7 minutes)
source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, Mars; light travel time calculation

text: The top ~3 m of the ocean holds as much heat as the whole atmosphere
as_written: The top three metres or so of the sea hold as much heat as the entire atmosphere
source: NOAA National Ocean Service

text: Earth reflects close to 30 percent of incoming sunlight (Bond albedo about 0.29 to 0.30)
source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet; NASA CERES

text: Earth's outgoing longwave radiation is roughly 240 W per square metre
as_written: roughly two hundred and forty watts per square metre
source: NASA CERES; Stephens et al. 2012, Nature Geoscience

text: Absorbed sunlight at Mars distance is about 100 W per square metre (1361 x 0.43 x 0.70 / 4 is about 102)
source: Derived from TSIS-1 irradiance, inverse square law, and NASA albedo

text: Earth's present energy imbalance is of order one to two W per square metre
source: NASA CERES; Loeb et al. 2021, Geophysical Research Letters

text: Earth's day length is about 24 hours
source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet

text: Earth's axial tilt is about 23.4 degrees
as_written: about twenty three and a half degrees
source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet

text: The Sun's tidal effect is a bit under half the Moon's (about 46 percent)
as_written: a bit under half the Moon's
source: NOAA National Ocean Service, Tides and Water Levels

text: Tidal force scales as the inverse cube of distance, so solar tides fall to about 28 percent of the present value at 1.52 AU
source: Newtonian tidal theory; derived

text: Saturation water vapour in air rises about 7 percent per degree Celsius (Clausius-Clapeyron)
as_written: about seven percent less water vapour
source: IPCC AR6 WG1 Chapter 8; Clausius-Clapeyron relation

text: Earth without an atmosphere would average about minus 18 C (255 K)
source: NASA Earth Observatory and NASA Climate; standard radiative equilibrium

text: Natural greenhouse effect warms Earth by about 33 C, giving a mean near 15 C
source: NASA Earth Observatory; IPCC AR6 WG1

text: Equilibrium temperature with no greenhouse at 43 percent sunlight and albedo 0.30 is about 207 K, or minus 66 C
source: Derived from Stefan-Boltzmann law with TSIS-1 irradiance and NASA Earth albedo

text: A year at Mars's distance is about 687 days (Kepler's third law)
as_written: about six hundred and eighty seven days
source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, Mars (686.98 days)

text: Each season lasts close to six months, about 172 days
source: Derived from a 687 day orbital period

text: World population is about eight billion
source: United Nations World Population Prospects 2022

text: Seawater freezes at about minus 1.8 C
as_written: about minus one point eight degrees Celsius
source: NOAA National Ocean Service; NSIDC

text: Fresh snow reflects more than 80 percent of sunlight
source: National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC)

text: Cryogenian glaciations occurred roughly 720 to 635 million years ago
as_written: seven hundred and twenty and six hundred and thirty five million years ago
source: Hoffman et al. 2017, Science Advances; Rooney et al. 2015

text: The Sun was about 6 percent dimmer around 700 million years ago
source: Gough 1981, Solar Physics; standard solar evolution models

text: Whether the Cryogenian Earth was a hard snowball or a slushball remains debated
source: Hoffman et al. 2017, Science Advances; Abbot, Voigt and Koll 2011

text: Coldest air temperature ever measured on Earth is minus 89.2 C at Vostok on 21 July 1983
as_written: minus eighty nine point two degrees Celsius
source: World Meteorological Organization Weather and Climate Extremes Archive

text: Lake Vostok lies under nearly 4 km of ice
source: Siegert et al. 2001, Nature; British Antarctic Survey

text: Outer edge of the habitable zone with a CO2 atmosphere is about 1.67 AU
as_written: about one point six seven times Earth's distance
source: Kopparapu et al. 2013, The Astrophysical Journal 765, 131

text: Mars is at about 1.52 AU
source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, Mars

text: Mars's surface pressure is under 1 percent of Earth's (about 0.6 percent)
as_written: less than one percent of Earth's
source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, Mars

text: Escape from snowball Earth requires CO2 hundreds of times the present level
source: Caldeira and Kasting 1992, Nature; Pierrehumbert 2004, Nature

text: Snowball episodes lasted a few million to tens of millions of years
as_written: from a few million years to tens of millions
source: Rooney et al. 2015, PNAS; Macdonald et al. 2010, Science

text: Homo sapiens is about 300,000 years old
as_written: about three hundred thousand years old
source: Hublin et al. 2017, Nature (Jebel Irhoud)

text: The early Sun was about 30 percent dimmer than today
source: NASA Astrobiology; Sagan and Mullen 1972, Science

text: How Earth stayed warm under the faint young Sun is still debated
source: Feulner 2012, Reviews of Geophysics
